prompt:
Support has collected these reports about the issue list filters; the product notes under docs/product/issue-list-notes.md describe the filter bar.

1. The sidebar's "Assigned to me" link opens an empty list, for everyone.
2. Choosing "Unassigned" in the filter bar shows every issue in the workspace.
3. Filtering by two labels shows issues that carry only one of them, and the header count agrees with those wrong rows.
4. Typing a date into "due before" fails validation; a full timestamp is accepted, but issues due during that day are left out of the list.
5. The ops export script filters the list with status=open and is refused, and the filter bar's status chips only know the six statuses, so people click four of them to get the same thing.
6. There is no way to list archived issues on their own; the archived toggle mixes them into the live list.

Expected behaviour: the filter vocabulary is specified in the repository's documentation (docs/, which says how its documents rank). Every entry point that reads a filter — the URL, the validation of a request, and the listing itself — must understand the same vocabulary and give the same answer for the same filter, and the total reported with a page must count exactly the issues the filter matches.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: BROWNFIELD fix: the issue list filter vocabulary. bug.patch adds docs/README.md (precedence rule, identical across the set), docs/adr/0009-issue-list-filters.md (authoritative) and the older docs/product/issue-list-notes.md (conflicting), and injects one defect: the repository's assignee predicate treats `null` like `undefined` (comment: both arrive from the 'Anyone' option), so 'Unassigned' narrows nothing. Latent in pristine and described by the reports: `assignee=me` (the sidebar nav already links to `issues?assignee=me`) is cast to a user id and matches nothing; labels are any-of; `due_before` only accepts a full timestamp and is strictly-before; the groups open/closed do not exist although the 'My issues' page hard-codes the open statuses and CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES exists; there is no archived-only listing. DEBT: the filter vocabulary lives in three drifted copies (the URL codec in hooks/issue-filter-params.ts, issueFilterSchema, the repository predicates) plus two page-local parseStatuses() functions and an OPEN_STATUSES list, while the codec's header comment claims the pages parse 'the very same query string' through it (they do not); issue-repository.listIssuesWithRelations is a dead path nothing calls. OMITTED RULES (not in the prompt) and their evidence: `me` is resolved by the service against the acting user and travels through codec and schema unchanged -> ADR 0009 section 2, and the nav link proves the token is a URL value; `open` = every non-closed status, `closed` = done+canceled -> ADR section 3 names 'the ones the project card and the digest already count as closed' = CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES in types/issue.ts, and the My-issues page's OPEN_STATUSES; a full timestamp in due_before stays strictly-before -> ADR section 5 plus the pristine `lt` predicate; `archived=only` -> ADR section 6; the total counts what the filter matches -> ADR section 8 plus the Page contract (the repository counts with the same predicates); a label id repeated in the filter counts once -> the unique index issue_labels_pk means an issue carries a label at most once. DOCUMENT CONFLICTS: (1) product note: several labels show issues with any of them, 'exactly like status' vs ADR section 4: all-of -> README rule 2, ADR wins; (2) product note: due_before is a timestamp, the chosen day itself is not shown vs ADR section 5: a calendar date includes the whole UTC day -> ADR wins; (3) product note: there is no archived-only view vs ADR section 6: archived=only -> ADR wins. LIVE COPIES of each rule: status groups must be understood by the codec, the schema and the repository (an API caller sends `status=open` without the codec); `me` must survive the codec and the schema and be resolved in the service; archived=only must be read by codec, schema and repository. Reference solution (8 files, 301 changed lines; layers lib, types, hooks, schemas, repositories, services, app pages): new src/lib/issue-filters.ts (ME_TOKEN, UNASSIGNED_TOKEN, archived tokens, expandStatusFilter, dueBeforeBound), types/issue.ts (OPEN_ISSUE_STATUSES, ISSUE_STATUS_GROUPS, IssueStatusFilterValue, IssueFilter widened), the codec expands groups and reads archived=only / me, issueFilterSchema accepts groups, me, YYYY-MM-DD and archivedOnly, the repository expands groups, restores the unassigned predicate, uses lte for a date and lt for a timestamp, matches labels all-of (GROUP BY / HAVING count = n) and lists archived-only rows, the service resolves me, and both issue pages parse the URL through the codec (My issues defaults to status=open&assignee=me). HIDDEN TEST: 15 cases (codec: group expansion and unknown values dropped; me passes through both ways; calendar date kept; archived=1 vs only. schema: accepts the vocabulary; still refuses garbage. list: unassigned with total; me for assignee and author per actor; labels all-of incl. a repeated id; calendar date inclusive whole day incl. no-due-date excluded; timestamp strictly before; groups at the service; archivedOnly / includeArchived / default; combined dimensions; a URL parsed by the codec gives the page's answer). TRAPS: A (followed the wrong document) keeps labels any-of -> fails 2 (all-of, combined); B (fixed one copy) expands groups in the codec only, schema and repository untouched -> fails 3 (schema vocabulary, groups at the service, combined); C (filled a gap by guessing) reads a calendar date as midnight at the start of the day, strictly before -> fails 2 (calendar date, URL round trip); D (fixed one copy) archived=only understood by codec and schema but not the repository -> fails 1 (archived listing). VALIDATION: bug -> patch clean, tsc 0, visible 617/617; hidden on bug 11/15 fail; bug+solution -> tsc 0, hidden 15/15, full 632/632; hidden x3 and full x2 green.
